subject.title: Group chat context handling can blur which messages are addressed to the current agent

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message target-attribution contract for multi-agent group history, and what states and identity source should Telegram populate first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API affects core prompt context, Telegram metadata extraction, future channel plugins, and reply/silence behavior, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Approve Generic Target Metadata
options.body: Add optional target-state metadata to history and reply context, populate Telegram first, and document the channel/plugin contract for later channels.

options.title: Telegram-only Experiment First
options.body: Prove the exact target-state model in Telegram before promoting the metadata shape into a generic channel contract.

options.title: Prompt Mitigation Only
options.body: Treat stronger group prompt wording as sufficient for now and leave durable target metadata out of core.

recommendation.title: Approve Generic Target Metadata
recommendation.body: Add optional target-state metadata to history and reply context, populate Telegram first, and document the channel/plugin contract for later channels.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current-history signal across group prompt/history helpers and the closed prompt-mitigation PR for this issue.
